content: The American College of Physicians (ACP) is a professional organization for internists, who are physicians specializing in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases in adults. With over 119,000 members, it is the largest medical specialty organization in the United States and the second-largest physician group overall. ACP supports its members by providing resources, advocacy, and education related to internal medicine and its subspecialties. Its membership includes not only practicing internists but also medical students, residents, and fellows. Members are actively involved in clinical practice, medical education, research, and healthcare administration. The mission of the ACP is to improve the quality and effectiveness of healthcare by promoting excellence and professionalism in the field of internal medicine. The organization was established in 1915 to advance the science and practice of medicine. In 1998, it merged with the American Society of Internal Medicine (ASIM), which had been founded in 1956 to address the economic aspects of medical practice. From 1998 to 2003, the combined organization was known as ACP-ASIM, but it later reverted to its original name, the American College of Physicians. The governance of ACP is overseen by a Board of Regents, which is elected by its members. This board is supported by various committees and the ACP Board of Governors, which includes 79 elected Governors representing chapters and regions across the United States, Canada, Central and South America, and Japan. The organization also sponsors the Council of Subspecialty Societies, which includes 25 subspecialty and internal medicine-related organizations. ACP is actively involved in broader medical communities, including the American Medical Association, the Federated Council for Internal Medicine, and the Council of Medical Specialty Societies. ACP offers several levels of membership, including Medical Student, Associate, Member, Fellow (FACP), Honorary Fellow, and Master (MACP). Fellowship and Mastership are honors that recognize exceptional contributions to internal medicine. Fellows are nominated by their peers and endorsed by local chapter leaders, while Masters are selected from among the Fellows for their distinguished achievements. Physician assistants who are members of the American Academy of Physician Assistants can also join ACP as Affiliate members. Membership is otherwise limited to physicians and medical students with an interest in internal medicine. While board certification in internal medicine is not mandatory for membership, applicants must be board eligible. Internists undergo three years of specialized training after medical school, focusing on adult diseases, while subspecialists complete additional training in fields such as cardiology, endocrinology, geriatrics, nephrology, gastroenterology, and infectious diseases. ACP publishes several highly regarded medical resources. The Annals of Internal Medicine, released biweekly, is one of the most frequently cited medical journals globally. The ACP Journal Club provides summaries of significant clinical articles from over 100 medical journals. The ACP Observer is a monthly newsmagazine for internists, and ACP Medicine is an evidence-based reference for internal medicine. Additionally, ACP produces a variety of books on healthcare and medical practice. The organization is actively involved in public policy and advocacy through its Washington, D.C., office, which addresses issues affecting public health and medical practice. ACP develops policy statements and engages with government entities to influence healthcare legislation and administration. The ACP Center for Ethics and Professionalism promotes ethical standards in medicine to enhance patient care. The ACP Foundation supports the organization’s mission by funding programs in education, research, service, and professionalism. ACP provides extensive educational resources for internists, including its Annual Session, a national scientific meeting with over 260 presentations. It also offers the Medical Knowledge Self-Assessment Program (MKSAP), now in its 13th edition, as well as board review courses, recertification courses, and regional meetings. For medical students and residents, ACP provides career guidance, the MKSAP for Students, and an In-Training Examination. Its electronic resources include PIER (Physicians’ Information and Education Resource), a web-based decision-support tool offering evidence-based guidance across more than 400 clinical areas. Other tools include MKSAP 13, MKSAP 13 Update, and a PDA portal. ACP also provides Clinical Skills Teaching Modules to enhance medical education. The ACP Practice Management Center offers practical resources, tools, and personalized advice to help members navigate the complexities of modern healthcare practice. The Medical Laboratory Evaluation Program (MLE) provides proficiency testing for laboratories in the U.S. and internationally. ACP also runs the Doctors For Adults® website, which offers patient education materials reviewed by ACP physicians and free of commercial endorsements. In 2007, ACP launched its Diabetes Portal, an interactive resource for both patients and clinicians.
